source.section: PDF page 9, Line 26 (Pensions of New York State and local governments and the federal government: New York State); Form IT-201 line 26; Form IT-201 lines 19, 24, 32-39 (PDF pages 2-3); IT-201-I PDF page 11 (line 34 standard deduction table), PDF pages 12 and 33 (line 39, rate schedule)

worked: Single, 58 (under 59 1/2: line 26 has no age test), wages 80,000 and a New York State Employees' Retirement System pension 60,000. Federal AGI 140,000, but New York AGI is what picks the tax computation, and after the subtraction it is under 107,650, so there is no recapture. Federal AGI (IT-201 line 19) = 140,000.00. Federal taxable income = 140,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 124,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtraction: line 26 New York State (NYS and Local Retirement System) pension, any age, no limit 60,000.00. Line 32 total subtractions = 60,000.00. Line 33 New York AGI = 140,000.00 - 60,000.00 = 80,000.00. Line 34 New York standard deduction (single, PDF page 11 table) 8,000.00; line 35 = 80,000.00 - 8,000.00 = 72,000.00; line 36 dependent exemption 0 (no dependents); lines 37/38 taxable income 72,000.00. Rate schedule (PDF page 33, single) on 72,000.00: 8,500.00 x 4% = 340.00; 3,200.00 x 4.5% = 144.00; 2,200.00 x 5.25% = 115.50; 58,100.00 x 5.5% = 3,195.50; schedule tax = 3,795.00 (the printed schedule, with its whole-dollar base 600 at 13,900, gives 3,795.50; this case uses the bands as numbers). NY AGI is 107,650 or less and line 38 is 65,000 or more: the rate schedule applies (PDF page 12, line 39); no recapture worksheet. Line 39 NYS tax = 3,795.00. Credits: none (the household credit, line 40, PDF page 12 tables 1-3, allows no credit above federal AGI of 28,000 single or 32,000 other statuses): state income tax = 3,795.00.
